verdicts.quote: exactly one user is created per data record, as one atomic unit: all appear or none do.
`rejected` shows "Nothing was imported", the error count and a table with columns Row, Field, Problem sorted by row
unique within the file compared case-insensitively (`duplicate_in_file`, also giving `first_row`); not already in the store, compared case-insensitively (`email_exists`).
The CSV cannot grant any role […] created users take the host default role.
verdicts.missing: The file cannot assign roles. The spec leaves open whether the host default can exceed the importer’s authority and how to handle that case.

verdicts.quote:
the import page and the import request are available only to an authenticated identity the host
  authorizes as admin.
verdicts.missing: The relationship between the host’s single-user creation permission and its admin grant is unspecified.

verdicts.quote:
first record is a header. […] against `email` and `name`; both are required, order is free, nothing
  else is allowed. […] header errors `missing_column`, `unknown_column`, `duplicate_column`

UTF-8 with
  an optional leading BOM that is stripped; comma delimiter; RFC 4180 double-quote quoting; LF or CRLF […] record `ada@example.com,"Lovelace, Ada"` is valid […] a record spanning several physical lines is one row.
A fault injected at the second insert of a valid file returns 500 `import_failed` and leaves S0. […] no third-party or remote service is called; no outbound email.

no default value is chosen […] Over `MAX_FILE_BYTES` the upload is rejected with 413 `file_too_large` […] more than `MAX_DATA_ROWS` data records is rejected 400 `too_many_rows` before any row validation.
verdicts.missing: The production byte and data-row limits still need values. The numeric fixtures apply only to tests.

verdicts.quote: empty body part returns 400 `file_empty`; `email,name` + LF returns 400 `no_rows` […] a one-row file `email,name` / `solo@example.com,Solo` returns 201 with created_count 1.
F-OK a second time against the store after AC-4.1 returns 422 with `(2,email,email_exists)` and `(3,email,email_exists)`; the store keeps 3 users and each name is unchanged.
the import request completes synchronously and its response is the only result carrier. […] No job queue, worker or status record.
verdicts.missing: The spec chooses synchronous processing for every accepted file. It provides no background processing or completion notification for a background import.

verdicts.quote: welcome or invitation email, and how new users first sign in (G-4) […] no outbound email.
how imported users first obtain credentials (invitation, reset link, none) and whether they are notified. This is a product decision for the user.
verdicts.missing: The initial account status, whether a password exists at creation, and the first sign-in flow remain unspecified.

verdicts.quote: Uploaded bytes live only in request memory (or a transient spool removed before the response is sent). […] Upload bytes | server request memory | no one | n/a, per request | the response is sent

event `user_import`, actor id, UTC timestamp, outcome (`created`, `rejected`, `denied`, `failed`),
  data-row count when parsed, created_count, and the distinct set of error codes.
a client that disconnects mid-upload leaves no partial effect […] no write; 422 with every error | fix and resend
verdicts.missing: The spec covers disconnects and whole-file retries. It gives no admin action to cancel work already running or retry just the failed rows.

verdicts.quote: an import of `MAX_DATA_ROWS` rows completes within the host runtime's request time limit; neither value is known […] button disabled, label "Importing", indeterminate indicator, no fabricated percentage
verdicts.missing: The pending indicator is specified. A measurable maximum duration for a maximum-size import still depends on the host timeout and the production limits.

verdicts.quote:
Import only creates. It never
  changes or replaces an existing user.
verdicts.missing: The spec does not require the existing manual single-user creation flow to keep its behavior.

verdicts.quote: any value the host would reject is also a row error `invalid_value` on that field. […] values are stored verbatim after trim; any later CSV export owns that risk
